references.text: The fundamental law concerning Hebrew slaves who shall serve for six years and be released in the seventh year, which Deuteronomy 15:12 expands upon and elaborates.
Provisions regarding Israelites who sell themselves due to poverty, with a focus on the Jubilee year as the time of release.
Jeremiah refers directly to this law concerning the release of Hebrew slaves after six years and criticizes the people for breaking this covenant.
Special provisions for female slaves, which Deuteronomy 15:12 includes by mentioning both the Hebrew man and woman.
The Jubilee year as a year of release, related to the principle of liberation after a specific period of time.
Paul urges Philemon to receive the runaway slave Onesimus as a brother, reflecting the biblical principle of freedom and brotherhood.
